lesson_title: The Whole Stadium Sees the Same Game
hook_text: Every seat on the curve sees the goal at exactly the same angle. That one fact is worth marks in Paper 2.
clip_script: You're in a circular stadium. The goal mouth is a chord — two posts on the circle. You're high up on the curve behind the halfway line, and your friend has a seat way along the same curve. Who sees the goal open wider? Nobody. From every single seat on that same arc, the goal mouth opens at exactly the same angle. Not roughly the same. Exactly. That's a theorem — angles in the same segment — and it's worth real marks in Paper 2. Now walk down to the centre spot. From the exact centre of the circle, the goal opens at double the angle of any seat on the far curve. Centre sees one forty? Every seat sees seventy. The centre always claims double. And one more: if the goal-chord runs straight through the centre — a full diameter — the centre's angle is a flat one eighty, so every seat sees... ninety. A perfect right angle, from anywhere on the curve. See a diameter in an exam diagram, and a free ninety is sitting there waiting for you. One stadium. Three theorems. Fifty marks of geometry suddenly making sense.
visual_style: A glowing circular stadium from above: sightlines fanning from seats to the goalposts, equal angles pulsing along one arc; the centre spot flaring at double width; a diameter snapping into place with a bright right-angle symbol at the curve.
mood: Big-match energy turned into geometry, satisfying and visual.
pacing: Quick scene-setting, a pause on 'Nobody.', then three theorem beats landing like replays.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and turn circle theorems into pictures you cannot forget.
